why_ai: Adversarial incidents with missing evidence drive notification and litigation; insurer panels pick trusted firms.
why_clarity: Scope is often only boundable, and whether conclusions held surfaces in litigation much later.
why_digital: Logs, images and telemetry in, reports out, engaged through insurer panels and counsel.

why_ai: A credentialed expert must personally defend attribution under cross-examination; courts will still require humans.
why_clarity: Attribution confidence is uncalibrated narrative, and each case is resolved by courts or insurers years later.
why_digital: Evidence is digital, but testimony is delivered in person and experts are chosen by reputation.

why_ai: Engagement letters, conflict checks and caps are repeatable administrative process software can run.
why_clarity: The same commercial shell recurs on every activation with defined documents and approvals.
why_digital: Contracts, panel terms and billing are documents handled remotely.

why_ai: Reasoning from partial evidence under a clock is consequential, but its structure is largely repeatable.
why_clarity: The method lives in practitioners' heads and whether a bound was right may never be known.
why_digital: Surviving logs and artefacts in, a stated bound out, all on screens.

why_ai: Comparing logging configuration to known evidence needs is a largely mechanical gap assessment.
why_clarity: A ranked gap list is well defined, but it is only proven right when an incident occurs.
why_digital: Logging configurations in, assessment reports out, delivered remotely.

why_ai: Mid-crisis investigation against an adversary under insurer panels stays human, though mobilisation automates.
why_clarity: Mobilisation steps repeat, but each investigation differs and conclusions are hard to verify quickly.
why_digital: Remote collection and analysis of digital evidence, bought via insurers and breach coaches.

why_ai: Report assembly, evidence binding and consistency checking are mechanical tasks AI handles well.
why_clarity: Each engagement produces the same report set from findings already established.
why_digital: Investigation records in, documents out, all on screens.

why_ai: The scope statement drives notification and litigation, and someone accountable must stand behind it.
why_clarity: What was accessed is often unknowable, so correctness is rarely checked objectively.
why_digital: Evidence analysis and statements are digital, bought by counsel and insurers.

why_ai: Advising inexperienced executives on notification under a statutory clock is trust-heavy and consequential.
why_clarity: Each crisis differs, and whether the notification call was right emerges later.
why_digital: Delivered through bridge calls and board meetings, sometimes in person.

why_ai: Senior responders investigating live adversaries are scarce, and AI-driven attacks grow demand.
why_clarity: Engagements share a pattern but each investigation is novel and slow to verify.
why_digital: Responders work on digital evidence remotely, staffed through firms and panels.

why_ai: Normalising formats and correlating clocks is mechanical work tooling will absorb.
why_clarity: Every case needs the same timeline built from parsed events, checkable against sources.
why_digital: Logs in, an event sequence out, built entirely in software.
